correctness.rationale: The point/line covering inequalities give gamma>=5, and the nine explicit S(x,z) sets and their nine duals give exactly all 18 minima. A representative fatal attack and incidence-automorphism orbit show no five-set is eternally defendable. Two independent exhaustive implementations enumerate all 18 choose 6 sets: precisely 423 dominate. They independently check 72,891 legal ordered six-guard transitions and all 5,076 six-state/attack pairs, with 25–81 valid destination configurations per attack. Induction on subsequent attacks proves gamma_infty^m<=6. Combined, the exact result is established. All finite bounds are exhaustive; no experiments are extrapolated to unrelated graphs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2005 broad equality claim is false according to the inspected 2016 correction; hence it is not valid broader coverage. The 2016 counterexample is a different graph of degree six. The 2015 work covers circulants, generalized Petersen graphs, binary trees and caterpillars and neither identifies the Pappus incidence graph nor implies its full six-guard response census.

originality.rationale: Exact Pappus 18-vertex cubic Cayley counterexample and the complete 423-state six-guard attack-response classification were compared with foundational 2005 and corrective 2016 primary full-text material, relevant 2015 graph-family literature, actual semantic mathematical-record queries and historical claim IDs. The 2005 universal Cayley equality was refuted in 2016, so it cannot invalidate the new computation as a correct theorem. The 2016 example is 6-regular and gives no cubic Pappus value. The 2015 families exclude this incidence graph. No stronger covering result was identified. Unindexed/undownloadable sources remain residual risk; independent priority certification not claimed.

value.rationale: A complete all-state m-eternal defense classification on a classical cubic vertex-transitive Cayley graph is mathematically motivated: it supplies a strict ordinary/eternal gap in smaller degree than the compared published explicit six-regular Cayley example, identifies every minimal-state obstruction and all six-guard winning states, and gives an exact robust strategy benchmark. It claims neither smallest possible graph order nor minimal degree among all graphs.
